quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Imagine something so ordinary it happens practically every day.
quests.explanation: Commonplace is correct — it means very ordinary, happening often, the opposite of unprecedented.
quests.textToSpeak: A power outage lasting an entire week felt *unprecedented* in our town.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: That's an event so routine that nobody thinks twice about it.
quests.explanation: Very ordinary, happening often, is commonplace, the reverse of unprecedented.
quests.textToSpeak: The school faced an *unprecedented* number of applications this year.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Consider a situation you've already seen play out dozens of times before.
quests.explanation: Unprecedented means never having happened before; commonplace, its opposite, means happening all the time.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Envision a salesperson who lies about a product just to close the sale.
quests.explanation: Unscrupulous is the word — it means willing to act dishonestly for personal gain, the opposite of scrupulous.
quests.textToSpeak: Choose a *scrupulous* travel agent who won't hide extra fees.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: This is someone who cheats on a test and shows no guilt about it.
quests.explanation: Willing to act dishonestly for personal gain is unscrupulous, the reverse of scrupulous.
quests.textToSpeak: My uncle is *scrupulous* about splitting the inheritance fairly.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Call to mind a company that knowingly overcharges its most loyal customers.
quests.explanation: Scrupulous means careful to act honestly and fairly; unscrupulous, its opposite, means willing to cheat for gain.
quests.textToSpeak: A *scrupulous* seller always describes an item's flaws honestly.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Think of a warning shouted directly at you, impossible to miss or misread.
quests.explanation: That's it — blatant. It means completely obvious, not hidden at all, the opposite of veiled.
quests.textToSpeak: The chef's *veiled* hint about the secret ingredient left us guessing.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: It's an announcement made in plain, unmistakable words.
quests.explanation: Completely obvious, not hidden at all, is blatant, the reverse of veiled.
quests.textToSpeak: The company made a *veiled* reference to an upcoming product.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Picture a sign that states exactly what it means, with nothing hidden.
quests.explanation: Veiled means partly hidden or disguised; blatant, its opposite, means impossible to miss.
quests.textToSpeak: The nurse gave a *veiled* warning about the risks of skipping meals.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Imagine a bridge that hasn't wobbled once in fifty years.
quests.explanation: Firm is right — it means solid and steady, not likely to fail, the opposite of precarious.
quests.textToSpeak: The stunt performer stood on a *precarious* ledge for the final scene.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: That's a job you're certain will still be there next year.
quests.explanation: Solid and steady, not likely to fail, is firm, the reverse of precarious.
quests.textToSpeak: That old ladder looks *precarious* - I wouldn't climb it.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Consider a table standing perfectly steady on all four legs.
quests.explanation: Precarious means unstable and likely to collapse or fail; firm, its opposite, means solid and secure.
quests.textToSpeak: Her grades put her in a *precarious* position before finals.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Envision someone who agrees to every new rule without any pushback.
quests.explanation: Compliant is correct — it means willing to obey or go along with something, the opposite of obstinate.
quests.textToSpeak: He remained *obstinate* about using the old software, despite the update.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: This is following instructions exactly as given, no arguments at all.
quests.explanation: Willing to obey or go along with something is compliant, the reverse of obstinate.
quests.textToSpeak: The customs officer was *obstinate* about checking every single bag.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Call to mind an employee who happily adjusts to whatever the manager asks.
quests.explanation: Obstinate means stubbornly refusing to change; compliant, its opposite, means willingly going along with things.
quests.textToSpeak: My grandfather can be *obstinate* about changing his daily routine.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.

quests.explanation: Calm and unconcerned, not bothered by details, is nonchalant, the reverse of fastidious.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Picture someone who couldn't care less if the cables were tangled.
quests.explanation: Fastidious means extremely attentive to detail; nonchalant, its opposite, means relaxed and unbothered by it.
quests.textToSpeak: He's *fastidious* about keeping his cables perfectly organized.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Imagine a gentle breeze that couldn't possibly hurt anyone.
quests.explanation: Exactly — harmless. It means causing no damage or harm, the opposite of pernicious.
quests.textToSpeak: Doctors warned about the *pernicious* effects of skipping sleep for weeks.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: That's a small habit with no real downside at all.
quests.explanation: Causing no damage or harm is harmless, the reverse of pernicious.
quests.textToSpeak: The show explored the *pernicious* influence of gossip in small towns.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Consider a spider so mild that its bite feels like nothing.
quests.explanation: Pernicious means gradually causing serious harm; harmless, its opposite, means causing none at all.
quests.textToSpeak: A *pernicious* habit like constant snacking can be hard to break.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.

quests.explanation: Verbose is right — it means using far more words than necessary, the opposite of laconic.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: This is a story that takes forever to get to the point.
quests.explanation: Using far more words than necessary is verbose, the reverse of laconic.
quests.textToSpeak: The manager's *laconic* emails rarely go beyond two short sentences.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: Call to mind someone who answers a simple yes-or-no question with a ten-minute speech.
quests.explanation: Laconic means using very few words; verbose, its opposite, means using far more than needed.
quests.textToSpeak: Our guide's *laconic* replies left us wanting more details about the ruins.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.

quests.explanation: Right — petty. It means overly concerned with small, unimportant things, the opposite of magnanimous.
quests.textToSpeak: My sister was *magnanimous* about letting her brother win the board game.

quests.instruction: Speak the opposite of the highlighted word.
quests.hint: It's refusing to share credit for even the tiniest part of a project.
quests.explanation: Overly concerned with small, unimportant things is petty, the reverse of magnanimous.
quests.textToSpeak: The manager was *magnanimous*, offering a refund without any questions.

quests.hint: Picture someone getting upset over one dollar in a group bill.
quests.explanation: Magnanimous means generous and forgiving, especially toward rivals; petty, its opposite, means small-minded about tiny things.
quests.textToSpeak: The chef was *magnanimous*, sharing his secret recipe with the whole class.

quests.explanation: Obvious is the word — it means easy to see or understand, the opposite of inscrutable.

quests.explanation: Easy to see or understand is obvious, the reverse of inscrutable.

quests.explanation: Inscrutable means impossible to interpret or read; obvious, its opposite, means easy to understand at a glance.
